name: Basic Chia Seed Pudding
description: A creamy, make-ahead pudding that requires zero cooking

timing.notes: Plus 1-2 hours (or overnight) refrigeration to set

equipment.item: Mason jar with lid OR medium bowl with cover

ingredients.notes: Coconut, almond, or cashew milk work well
Optional - can substitute honey or omit

prep_steps.instruction: Set up your staging area: get out a mason jar with lid (or a medium bowl with cover), measuring cups and spoons, a fork or whisk, and a small bowl for berries.
prep_steps.notes: Mason jar makes mixing and storing easier - you can shake it

prep_steps.instruction: Measure chia seeds into the mason jar or bowl
Measure milk, maple syrup, and vanilla extract - can add directly to jar or have ready in measuring cup
Wash berries and place in small bowl. Set aside in refrigerator for topping.

cook_steps.instruction: Add milk, maple syrup, and vanilla to the jar with chia seeds. If using a mason jar, secure lid and shake vigorously. If using a bowl, whisk well to combine.

cues.visual: Mixture is evenly combined, no dry clumps of chia

cook_steps.instruction: Let mixture sit for 5 minutes at room temperature

cues.visual: Chia seeds beginning to absorb liquid and swell

cook_steps.instruction: Stir or shake again to break up any clumps that have formed
cook_steps.warnings: This step is important - clumps won't break up once fully set

cook_steps.instruction: Cover and refrigerate for 1-2 hours or overnight until set to a pudding-like consistency

cues.visual: Thick, pudding-like consistency. Seeds are fully hydrated and gel-like.

finishing.instructions: Divide pudding between two bowls. Top with fresh berries. Can also add: sliced banana, granola, nut butter, coconut flakes, or cacao nibs.
finishing.make_ahead: This IS a make-ahead recipe. Prep the night before for easy breakfast.
finishing.storage: Keeps refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 5 days. Stir before serving as it may thicken further.

notes: Full-fat coconut milk makes the creamiest pudding
If too thick after setting, stir in a splash more milk
Can be portioned into individual jars for grab-and-go breakfast
